## Latest Stable Version: Next.js 16.1

Next.js 16.1 was released on December 18th, 2025.(no content)This release focuses on faster development workflows and improved stability, with major updates to Turbopack and tooling.

### Key Features in Next.js 16.1:
- Turbopack File System Caching for `next dev` (now stable), Next.js Bundle Analyzer (experimental), and easier debugging with `next dev --inspect`.
- Turbopack file system caching for next dev is now stable and on by default. Compiler artifacts are stored on disk, leading to significantly faster compile times when restarting your development server, especially in large projects.
- Next.js installs are about 20MB smaller thanks to simplifications in the Turbopack file system caching layer.

## Next.js 16 (Released October 2025)

Next.js 16 was released ahead of Next.js Conf 2025, providing the latest improvements to Turbopack, caching, and the Next.js architecture.

### Major Features in Next.js 16:
- Turbopack has officially graduated from beta and is now the default bundler for all new Next.js projects. It's fast, like 2–5× faster builds and up to 10× faster Fast Refresh.
- Unlike the implicit caching found in previous versions of the App Router, caching with Cache Components is entirely opt-in. All dynamic code in any page, layout, or API route is executed at request time by default.
- The App Router in Next.js 16 uses the latest React Canary release, which includes the newly released React 19.2 features.
- Next.js DevTools MCP hooks into the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which lets AI tools and agents understand your project's context, your routing, caching, and rendering behaviour.

### Breaking Changes in Next.js 16:
- Node.js: The minimum version is now 20.9.0 (LTS). Node.js 18 is no longer supported. TypeScript: The minimum version is now 5.1.0.

### Security Note:
Two vulnerabilities have been identified in React Server Components: a high-severity Denial of Service (CVE-2025-55184) and a medium-severity Source Code Exposure (CVE-2025-55183). All Next.js 13.x, 14.x, 15.x and 16.x users should upgrade immediately.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The conversation is summarized below:
Analysis:
Let me chronologically analyze the conversation:

1. **First Request - Hero Card Transparency Issue**: User had a card in the hero section with a decorative border that was visible through the main card due to transparency. I fixed it by adding an opaque background layer.

2. **Second Request - Navbar Transparency**: User reported the navbar and Services dropdown were transparent when scrolling. I created a new CSS class `glass-panel-solid` with opaque background.

3. **Third Issue - Wrong CSS Variable**: The `glass-panel-solid` used `--dark` which didn't exist. User said it still didn't work. Fixed by using `--bg` variable.

4. **Fourth Request - Match Green Background**: User wanted the header to match the page's green-tinted background. Changed to `#0f1111` hex color.

5. **Fifth Request - Light Mode Card Styling**: User wanted the hero code card to look better in light mode - white with green border. Created CSS classes: `hero-code-card`, `hero-status-tag`, `hero-code-bg`, `hero-eyebrow-badge` with light mode variants.

6. **Sixth Request - Text Gradient in Light Mode**: User wanted "Un partenaire." text to be black in light mode. Added light mode variant for `.text-gradient`.

7. **Seventh Request - Remove Expert Photos**: User wanted to remove the "+15 experts" section with photos (only 4 experts), replace with "4 experts disponibles maintenant". Updated component and translations.

8. **Eighth Request - Expertise Page Technologies**: User wanted 15+ technical expertise cards added to the expertise page. Added technologies across frontend, backend, AI, mobile, and infra categories.

9. **Ninth Request - More Technologies + Orbit Logos**: User wanted React Native, Vercel, Resend, NeonDB, Supabase, Cloudflare, OVH, Stripe, Prisma, Figma added. Also wanted more logos in the hero orbit animation.

10. **Tenth Request (Most Recent)** - Update Versions + Fix Logos**: User noted versions were outdated (Next.js showed 14.2, should be 16.1). Also needed logos for OpenAI and Stripe.

Key technical patterns:
- CSS theming using `html[data-theme="light"]` selectors
- Devicon CDN for technology logos
- Simple Icons CDN for logos not in Devicon
- next-intl for translations
- Framer Motion for animations
- GlassPanel component for card styling

Files modified:
- `/src/components/sections/hero-home.tsx` - Hero section with code card
- `/src/app/globals.css` - CSS classes for theming
- `/src/components/site/header.tsx` - Navbar styling
- `/src/app/[locale]/expertise/page.tsx` - Main expertise page with technologies
- `/src/messages/fr.json` and `en.json` - Translations

Current work was updating all technology versions to latest and fixing logos for OpenAI/Stripe using Simple Icons CDN.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Fix transparency issues on hero card and navbar in dark mode
   - Style hero card and components properly for light mode (white background, green borders)
   - Update hero text gradient to black in light mode
   - Replace "+15 experts" section with "4 experts disponibles maintenant" (remove photos)
   - Add 15+ technology expertise cards to the `/fr/expertises` page with proper categories
   - Add 10 more technologies (React Native, Vercel, Resend, NeonDB, Supabase, Cloudflare, OVH, Stripe, Prisma, Figma)
   - Add 5 more logos in orbit animation in expertise hero
   - **Most Recent**: Update ALL technology versions to latest (e.g., Next.js 14.2 → 16.1) and find proper logos for OpenAI and Stripe

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - CSS theming with `html[data-theme="light"]` and `html[data-theme="dark"]` selectors
   - Devicon CDN (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/devicons/devicon/icons/`)
   - Simple Icons CDN (`cdn.simpleicons.org/`) for logos not in Devicon
   - GlassPanel component with glassmorphism effects
   - next-intl for i18n with `useTranslations` hook
   - Framer Motion for `animate-float` and parallax effects
   - CSS variables: `--bg`, `--glass-bg`, `--glass-border`, `--primary`

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`/src/app/[locale]/expertise/page.tsx`** - Main expertise page
     - Contains `techData` array with all 30 technologies
     - Icon mapping using conditional logic for Devicon vs Simple Icons
     - Hero with orbit logos using `animate-float`
     ```typescript
     src={
       {
         // Simple Icons (pour les logos non disponibles dans Devicon)
         openai: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/openai/white",
         stripe: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/stripe/white",
         langchain: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/langchain/white",
         supabase: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/supabase/white",
         vercel: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/vercel/white",
         cloudflare: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/cloudflare/white",
         neon: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/neon/white",
         resend: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/resend/white",
       }[tech.id] ||
       `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/devicons/devicon/icons/${...}.svg`
     }
     ```

   - **`/src/app/globals.css`** - Global styles
     - Added `glass-panel-solid` class for opaque backgrounds
     - Added hero-specific classes for light mode
     ```css
     .glass-panel-solid {
       background: #0f1111;
       backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
       border: 1px solid rgb(var(--glass-border));
     }
     html[data-theme="light"] .glass-panel-solid {
       background: #fafbfc;
     }
     html[data-theme="light"] .text-gradient {
       background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0f1111 0%, rgba(15,17,17,0.8) 100%);
     }
     ```

   - **`/src/components/sections/hero-home.tsx`** - Hero section
     - Updated code card with `hero-code-card` class
     - Replaced expert avatars with badge showing "4 Experts disponibles maintenant"

   - **`/src/components/site/header.tsx`** - Site header
     - Changed `glass-panel` to `glass-panel-solid` for navbar and Services dropdown

   - **`/src/messages/fr.json`** and **`/src/messages/en.json`**
     - Updated `hero.experts.available` translation key

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Navbar still transparent after adding `bg-dark`**: CSS specificity issue - `glass-panel` had inline background. Fix: Created new `glass-panel-solid` class that overrides the background.
   - **`--dark` variable doesn't exist**: Used wrong CSS variable. Fix: Changed to `--bg` then to hardcoded `#0f1111`.
   - **Expert photos showing wrong number**: User has 4 experts, not 15. Fix: Removed photos entirely, added simple badge with "4".
   - **`pytorch` and `aarch64` IDs for LangChain/OpenAI**: Confusing IDs that didn't match icon names. Fix: Changed to `langchain` and `openai` IDs.
   - **Missing logos for OpenAI, Stripe, etc.**: Devicon doesn't have all logos. Fix: Used Simple Icons CDN for those specific technologies.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved transparency issues by creating dedicated opaque CSS classes
   - Solved light mode styling by adding `html[data-theme="light"]` CSS selectors
   - Solved missing icons by using dual CDN approach (Devicon + Simple Icons)
   - Updated all 30 technology versions based on web searches for latest releases

6. All user messages:

  1703→      "content": [

  1710→    "waf-efficacite": {
  1711→      "title": "How to maximize a Web Application Firewall (WAF)?",
  1712→      "excerpt": "A well-configured WAF is the difference between symbolic protection and a real barrier.",
  1713→      "category": "Tech",
  1714→      "date": "Dec 11, 2025",
  1715→      "readTime": "6 min",
  1716→      "author": "Molly Allerhand",
  1717→      "content": [
  1718→        "A WAF blocks what it recognizes. Poor configuration leads to false positives or missed attacks.",
  1719→        "Start with observation mode and analyze logs to understand real traffic patterns.",
  1720→        "Tailor rules to critical routes, business use cases and your sector's attack patterns.",
  1721→        "Automate rule updates and add security regression tests to your CI/CD pipeline.",
  1722→        "Measure impact: block rate, latency, false positives and incidents avoided."
  1723→      ]
  1724→    },
  1725→    "integrite-logs-continu": {
  1726→      "title": "Certifying the integrity of a continuous log stream",
  1727→      "excerpt": "Proving your logs were not altered is now a security and compliance must.",
  1728→      "category": "Tech",
  1729→      "date": "Dec 11, 2025",
  1730→      "readTime": "7 min",
  1731→      "author": "Molly Allerhand",
  1732→      "content": [
  1733→        "Logs are evidence. You must be able to prove they have not been modified.",
  1734→        "The approach chains events with hashes and periodically signs the stream.",
  1735→        "Immutable storage (WORM) and timestamping reinforce traceability.",
  1736→        "A well-designed pipeline enables faster audits and stronger compliance (ISO, SOC2).",
  1737→        "We implement these guarantees on modern stacks without harming performance."
  1738→      ]
  1739→    },
  1740→    "mvp-iteration": {
  1741→      "title": "MVP and Iteration: The Right Approach",
  1742→      "excerpt": "How to build an effective minimum viable product and iterate intelligently.",
  1743→      "category": "Product",
  1744→      "date": "December 20, 2024",
  1745→      "readTime": "8 min",
  1746→      "author": "Yoann Andrieux",
  1747→      "content": [
  1748→        "The MVP concept is often misunderstood. It's not about delivering a sloppy product, but creating the simplest version that validates a hypothesis.",
  1749→        "The key is identifying the core value of your product. What makes it unique and essential? This is the core feature the MVP should focus on.",
  1750→        "Define clear metrics before launching. Without success criteria, you won't know how to interpret results and decide what's next.",
  1751→        "Iteration should be fast and data-driven. Analyze user behaviors, gather qualitative feedback, and prioritize ruthlessly.",
  1752→        "Don't be afraid to pivot if the data suggests it. An MVP that fails isn't a failure, it's valuable learning that brings you closer to product-market fit."
  1753→      ]
  1754→    },
  1755→    "core-web-vitals": {
  1756→      "title": "Core Web Vitals: A Practical Guide",
  1757→      "excerpt": "Everything about web performance metrics and how to optimize them.",
  1758→      "category": "Performance",
  1759→      "date": "December 15, 2024",
  1760→      "readTime": "10 min",
  1761→      "author": "Yoann Andrieux",
  1762→      "content": [
  1763→        "Core Web Vitals have become a Google ranking factor. But beyond SEO, they reflect user experience quality.",
  1764→        "LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) measures perceived loading time. Goal: under 2.5 seconds. Optimize your images, use lazy loading, and preload critical resources.",
  1765→        "FID (First Input Delay) measures responsiveness. Goal: under 100ms. Reduce blocking JavaScript and use code splitting.",
  1766→        "CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) measures visual stability. Goal: under 0.1. Reserve space for images and avoid dynamic content injections.",
  1767→        "Essential tools: Lighthouse for auditing, WebPageTest for detailed diagnostics, and Chrome DevTools for debugging. Measure in real conditions, not just locally.",
  1768→        "Optimization is an ongoing process. Integrate performance tests into your CI/CD and monitor regressions."
  1769→      ]
  1770→    },
  1771→    "owasp-2024": {
  1772→      "title": "Web Security: OWASP Top 10 in Practice",
  1773→      "excerpt": "The most common vulnerabilities and how to protect your applications.",
  1774→      "category": "Security",
  1775→      "date": "December 10, 2024",
  1776→      "readTime": "12 min",
  1777→      "author": "Yoann Andrieux",
  1778→      "content": [
  1779→        "Security is not optional. The OWASP Top 10 lists the most critical vulnerabilities every developer should know.",
  1780→        "Injections (SQL, NoSQL, LDAP) remain at the top. Always use parameterized queries and rigorously validate user input.",
  1781→        "Broken authentication is a classic. Implement 2FA, use proven libraries, and never reinvent the wheel with passwords.",
  1782→        "Sensitive data exposure can be fatal. Encrypt in transit (HTTPS) and at rest, minimize stored data, and regularly audit your endpoints.",
  1783→        "Vulnerable components are an often-neglected risk. Keep your dependencies up to date, use automated audit tools like Snyk or Dependabot.",
  1784→        "Security is everyone's business. Train your teams, integrate security tests into your pipeline, and have critical applications audited by experts."
  1785→      ]
  1786→    },
  1787→    "measuring-ai-roi-2026": {
  1788→      "title": "Measuring AI ROI in 2026: a pragmatic guide",
  1789→      "excerpt": "How to calculate real ROI for LLM adoption in SMBs.",
  1790→      "category": "AI & LLM",
  1791→      "date": "Jan 18, 2026",
  1792→      "readTime": "9 min",
  1793→      "author": "Alexandre V.",
  1794→      "content": [
  1795→        "AI ROI isn't a promise: without a clear frame, pilots get confused with business value.",
  1796→        "Start by listing total costs: inference, data ingestion, MLOps, security and monitoring.",
  1797→        "Measure productivity gains on defined tasks: time saved, errors avoided, SLA uplift.",
  1798→        "Compute incremental ROI per use case and prioritize those with payback under 12 months.",
  1799→        "Avoid hidden costs: data quality work, unnecessary fine-tuning and redundant tooling.",
  1800→        "Track mixed metrics: direct savings plus customer value (NPS, conversion, churn).",
  1801→        "Successful AI adoption behaves like a product: iterate, measure, govern."
  1802→      ]
  1803→    }
